note: Scripture source: the Indian Revised Version (IRV Hindi, CC BY-SA 4.0, Bridge Connectivity Solutions), fetched as USX from the ebible mirror (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/hin_irv/usx), all 66 books, 31,104 verses; section headings, acrostic letters and speaker labels stripped, and the IRV's editorial cross-references (e.g. '(यूह. 1:29)') dropped. Every quotation was inserted from that text by script, never typed. The English is Ochorus's MODERNISED edition and quotes a modern English Bible; the IRV decides the Hindi wording.

Derived by measurement: a row is mined only when the translator reported the quotation verbatim AND the reported Hindi segment (quote marks stripped, 6+ characters) is a substring of the cited IRV verse or range, and was found in the chapter body at block_index. 4 short verbatim claims failed that test (Ps 62:6, 37:23 in ch20; Ps 139:5, 139:16 in ch22) and ship self_rendered, as do all adapted rows (pronoun/person shifts, partial spans, quote marks re-placed to mirror the English).

Title and names agree with the shipped Hindi corpus: the book is सुखी जीवन का मसीही रहस्य — the title its own Hindi guide article (the-christians-secret-of-a-happy-life-guide.hi) and the hubs prose already use. NOTE: the hannah-whitall-smith Hindi bio, short bio, faq and export bio call it मसीही के सुखी जीवन का रहस्य; they were not changed in this PR. The author is हन्ना व्हिटॉल स्मिथ. Phrases the guide article already quotes from this book (मसीह के साथ परमेश्वर में छिपा हुआ जीवन; मनुष्य का भाग भरोसा रखना है और परमेश्वर का भाग कार्य करना है) are reused verbatim.

IRV/English divergences an editor should see: Job 13:15 — the IRV reads मुझे कुछ आशा नहीं, the opposite of 'yet I will hope in him', so ch18 self-renders चाहे वह मुझे घात करे, तो भी मैं उस पर आशा रखूँगा, the wording सब प्रकार की शान्ति का परमेश्वर.hi already ships; Luke 17:21 (ch19) is quoted verbatim as तुम्हारे बीच में ('among you') although the chapter's argument leans on 'within you' — a reviewer may prefer तुम्हारे भीतर; Matt 6:28 keeps the IRV's own spelling न काटते inside the quotation (the corpus does the same) while the author's prose uses कातते ('spin'); Acts 3:26 IRV अपने सेवक where the English says 'His Son Jesus' (ch02, IRV kept); Isa 9:7 copied as the IRV prints it, including what look like typos (ओर, सेनाओं के और यहोवा) (ch19); Rom 4:20 keeps the IRV's spelling संदेह inside the quotation.

Conventions: the reader is addressed as तुम (as in the author's shipped सब प्रकार की शान्ति का परमेश्वर.hi); God in prayer as तू; the author's first person takes feminine agreement; 'trial(s)' (hardship) is क्लेश in the author's prose, while परीक्षा is reserved for temptation and appears for 'trial' only inside IRV quotations of James 1 and 1 Peter 1; consecration/surrender समर्पण, entire consecration पूर्ण समर्पण; traditional spellings (शान्ति, सन्देह, आनन्द, परन्तु); curly quotation marks mirror the English per chapter, including its unbalanced marks (the English's straight-apostrophe inner quotes become ‘ ’); Roman rule numerals (I.–VII.) are written 1.–7.; chapter titles pinned across all translators.

Narration corrected in the Hindi (the English modernisation's slips, reported): ch08 'Pharaoh's wife' → पोतीपर की पत्नी (Potiphar's, as Genesis 39 and the 1875 original have it); ch03 five sentences whose modernised wording reverses the original ('Abandon all ease and comfort', 'If nothing could grieve', 'nor yet someone feeds him', 'Yet, he plans his life', 'She took them back') follow the original's sense. Citations kept as the English prints them even where wrong (e.g. ch05 Rom 12:12 for 12:1, ch08 2 Cor 2:14 for 3:14 and Heb 3:5-6, ch20 Ps 40:1 for 37:23 and 2 Kings 19:23 for Isa 31:1); each is in the PR's Found-not-fixed list.
AI-translated (ai_unreviewed), job #7545; 22 chapters translated by parallel agents under one conventions file, then reconciled for titles, terms, spelling and reader address across the whole book.
